meta.source: 原子序、符號、中英文名稱:常見週期表資料;原子量:已逐一對照 IUPAC CIAAW《Standard Atomic Weights 2024》與 NIST《Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions》(2026-11-13 查證);分類、版面位置:依教科書常見的分法與排列;電子殼層排列:已對照 NIST 資料(經 Wikipedia 轉引,少數元素的電子排列是例外,已逐一寫出);顏色:CPK 慣例配色;趣味小知識:自行撰寫。
meta.note: 原子量寫的是常用的簡約值(約 4~6 位有效數字);H、Li、B、C、N、O、Mg、Si、S、Cl、Br、Tl、Pb、Ar 在 IUPAC 表上是「區間」(隨自然界同位素組成而變),這裡取常規值,O 的 15.999 與 Tl 的 204.38 是區間四捨五入後的簡約值。沒有穩定同位素的元素沒有標準原子量,寫的是慣例用的質量數:Tc、Pm、Po 到 Pu 與 NIST 表一致;Am 以後以及 104~118 號是常見週期表的慣例值,超重元素(Bh、Hs、Mt、Ds、Rg、Cn、Fl)與 IAEA 核種資料裡半衰期最長的同位素不同,屬於慣例差異,不是錯誤。Zr、Gd 依 IUPAC 2024 修訂。電子殼層排列已於 2026-11-13 逐一對照 Wikipedia「Electron configurations of the elements」資料頁(其 1~104 號引用 NIST《Ground levels and ionization energies》與 Martin & Wiese《Atomic Spectroscopy》),118 個元素全部一致,包含銅、鉻、鈀、釓等例外排列;注意這是二手來源,NIST 原表因網站改版暫時取不到。103 號鐒在 NIST 與 CRC 都標為存疑;109~118 號從未實測,是理論預測值。radius 只是畫面用的示意大小,不是真實原子半徑;沒有寫的元素用殼層數估算。use 只有中文:英文版把知識與用途合成一句寫在 fact。

desc.zh: 不是金屬的元素,摸起來不閃亮、不太會導電。我們呼吸的氧、水裡的氫、鉛筆芯的碳都是非金屬,它們是生命的基本材料!
desc.en: Elements that are not metals: not shiny and they do not carry electricity well. Oxygen we breathe, hydrogen in water and carbon in pencils are nonmetals - the building blocks of life!

descTeen.zh: 非金屬通常不太導電、不太導熱,固體時很脆。它們容易和別的原子共用電子形成共價鍵,像碳、氧、氮、硫都是。
descTeen.en: Nonmetals usually conduct heat and electricity poorly, and solids are brittle. They readily share electrons to form covalent bonds, like carbon, oxygen, nitrogen and sulfur.

descHigh.zh: 非金屬(本表不含鹵素與稀有氣體)的電負度較高,傾向得到或共用電子;固體多為不良導體(石墨是常見的例外)。
descHigh.en: Nonmetals (here excluding the halogens and noble gases) have high electronegativity and tend to gain or share electrons; solids are mostly poor conductors (graphite is a common exception).

desc.zh: 最「害羞」的氣體家族,幾乎不跟別人牽手(不起反應)。氦氣讓氣球飄起來,氖氣讓招牌發光!
desc.en: The shy gas family: they almost never bond with others. Helium lifts balloons and neon makes signs glow!

descTeen.zh: 稀有氣體的最外層電子已經填滿(氦是 2 個、其他是 8 個),所以非常穩定,幾乎不和其他元素反應。
descTeen.en: The outer shell of a noble gas is full (2 electrons for helium, 8 for the others), so they are very stable and hardly react with other elements.

descHigh.zh: 稀有氣體的最外層為填滿的殼層(氦為 1s²,其餘為 ns²np⁶),化學性質極不活潑;較重的稀有氣體(如氙)在特殊條件下可以形成化合物。
descHigh.en: Noble gases have a filled outer shell (1s² for helium, ns²np⁶ for the rest) and are extremely unreactive; heavier ones such as xenon can form compounds under special conditions.

desc.zh: 又軟又活潑的金屬,軟到可以用刀切,遇到水會噗噗冒泡甚至爆炸!像鈉(食鹽裡有它)、鉀。
desc.en: Soft, super-active metals you can cut with a knife. In water they fizz or even explode! Like sodium (in table salt) and potassium.

descTeen.zh: 鹼金屬(不含氫)最外層只有 1 個電子,很容易失去,所以非常活潑,遇水會劇烈反應,通常保存在油裡。
descTeen.en: Alkali metals (not counting hydrogen) have just 1 outer electron, which they lose easily, so they are very reactive and react violently with water. They are usually stored under oil.

descHigh.zh: 第 1 族(氫除外)的金屬,價電子組態為 ns¹,第一游離能低,容易形成 +1 價陽離子;與水反應生成氫氧化物和氫氣,活性由上往下增強。
descHigh.en: The group 1 metals (except hydrogen) have the valence configuration ns¹ and a low first ionization energy, readily forming +1 ions. They react with water to give hydroxides and hydrogen, with reactivity increasing down the group.

desc.zh: 比鹼金屬穩重一點的金屬家族,像鈣(骨頭和牙齒)、鎂(煙火的亮白光)。
desc.en: Metals a bit calmer than the alkali family, like calcium (bones and teeth) and magnesium (bright white fireworks).

descTeen.zh: 鹼土金屬最外層有 2 個電子,容易失去而形成 +2 價的離子,比鹼金屬溫和一些。鈣是骨頭和牙齒的重要成分。
descTeen.en: Alkaline earth metals have 2 outer electrons and readily form +2 ions; they are milder than the alkali metals. Calcium is an important part of bones and teeth.

descHigh.zh: 第 2 族金屬,價電子組態為 ns²,常形成 +2 價離子;活性比同週期的鹼金屬低,由上往下逐漸增強。
descHigh.en: The group 2 metals have the valence configuration ns² and usually form +2 ions; they are less reactive than the alkali metals of the same period, with reactivity increasing down the group.

desc.zh: 我們最熟悉的硬金屬,又硬又亮又會導電。鐵、銅、金、銀都在這一家,可以做成房子、電線和珠寶!
desc.en: The hard, shiny metals we know best. Iron, copper, gold and silver are here - used for buildings, wires and jewelry!

descTeen.zh: 過渡金屬像鐵、銅、金,通常堅硬、有金屬光澤、很會導電導熱,它們的化合物常常有鮮豔的顏色。
descTeen.en: Transition metals such as iron, copper and gold are usually hard and shiny and conduct heat and electricity well. Their compounds are often brightly colored.

descHigh.zh: 過渡金屬的 d 軌域逐漸填入電子,常有多種氧化數,形成有顏色的化合物與錯合物,也常作為催化劑。
descHigh.en: In transition metals the d orbitals are progressively filled. They often have several oxidation states, form colored compounds and complexes, and are common catalysts.

desc.zh: 比較軟、熔點比較低的金屬,像鋁(鋁罐、鋁箔紙)、錫、鉛。
desc.en: Softer metals that melt more easily, like aluminum (cans and foil), tin and lead.

descTeen.zh: 貧金屬像鋁、錫、鉛,是比較軟的金屬,熔點比過渡金屬低,金屬的性質也比較弱。
descTeen.en: Post-transition metals such as aluminium, tin and lead are softer metals with lower melting points than the transition metals, and weaker metallic character.

descHigh.zh: 貧金屬(後過渡金屬)位於過渡金屬與類金屬之間,多半較軟、熔點較低,金屬性比過渡金屬弱。
descHigh.en: The post-transition metals sit between the transition metals and the metalloids; they are mostly soft with relatively low melting points and weaker metallic character.

desc.zh: 一半像金屬、一半像非金屬的「混血兒」。矽就是它,電腦和手機的晶片都靠它!
desc.en: Half metal, half nonmetal! Silicon is one - computer and phone chips are made from it.

descTeen.zh: 類金屬像矽、鍺,性質介於金屬和非金屬之間,導電力不錯但不如金屬,是製作電腦晶片的重要材料。
descTeen.en: Metalloids such as silicon and germanium lie between metals and nonmetals. They conduct electricity, but not as well as metals, and are key materials for computer chips.

descHigh.zh: 類金屬位於金屬與非金屬的分界線附近,導電性介於導體與絕緣體之間,可作半導體(如 Si、Ge)。
descHigh.en: Metalloids lie along the boundary between metals and nonmetals. Their conductivity is between that of conductors and insulators, so they can act as semiconductors (e.g. Si, Ge).

desc.zh: 很愛搶別人電子的活潑元素,會跟金屬變成鹽。氯可以幫游泳池殺菌,氟會保護牙齒。
desc.en: Active elements that love grabbing electrons and make salts with metals. Chlorine cleans pools and fluorine protects teeth.

descTeen.zh: 鹵素(氟、氯、溴、碘)最外層有 7 個電子,很想再得到 1 個,所以很活潑,常和金屬形成鹽類,例如食鹽(氯化鈉)。
descTeen.en: Halogens (fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine) have 7 outer electrons and want 1 more, so they are very reactive and often form salts with metals, such as table salt (sodium chloride).

descHigh.zh: 第 17 族,價電子組態為 ns²np⁵,容易得到 1 個電子成為 −1 價陰離子;單質為雙原子分子,氧化力由 F₂ 到 I₂ 逐漸減弱。
descHigh.en: Group 17 has the valence configuration ns²np⁵ and readily gains one electron to form −1 ions. The elements are diatomic molecules, and their oxidizing power decreases from F₂ to I₂.

desc.zh: 一群長得很像的稀土金屬,手機螢幕和強力磁鐵會用到它們。
desc.en: A group of similar rare-earth metals used in phone screens and strong magnets.

descTeen.zh: 鑭系元素(原子序 57 到 71)性質彼此很像,常用在強力磁鐵、螢光材料和電子產品。
descTeen.en: The lanthanides (atomic numbers 57 to 71) are very similar to one another and are used in strong magnets, phosphors and electronics.

descHigh.zh: 鑭系(La 到 Lu)的 4f 軌域逐漸填入電子,化學性質相近,最常見的氧化數是 +3;用於磁鐵、發光材料與催化劑。
descHigh.en: In the lanthanides (La to Lu) the 4f orbitals are progressively filled. Their chemistry is similar, with +3 the most common oxidation state; they are used in magnets, phosphors and catalysts.

desc.zh: 很重、大多帶有放射性的金屬,像鈾(核能發電的燃料)。很多是人造的,要小心使用!
desc.en: Heavy, mostly radioactive metals like uranium (fuel for nuclear power). Many are man-made and must be handled carefully!

descTeen.zh: 錒系元素(原子序 89 到 103)都有放射性,其中鈾和鈽可以用在核能發電。
descTeen.en: All the actinides (atomic numbers 89 to 103) are radioactive; uranium and plutonium are used in nuclear power.

descHigh.zh: 錒系(Ac 到 Lr)的 5f 軌域逐漸填入電子,全部具有放射性;鈾與鈽是重要的核燃料。
descHigh.en: In the actinides (Ac to Lr) the 5f orbitals are progressively filled and all are radioactive; uranium and plutonium are important nuclear fuels.

fact.zh: 宇宙裡最多、最輕的元素!太陽就是靠氫變成氦在發光。
fact.en: The most common element in the universe. The Sun shines by turning hydrogen into helium.

use.zh: 氫氣可以讓氣球飄起來,也能當燃料電池的能量來源。

factTeen.zh: 宇宙中最多、最輕的元素;太陽的能量來自氫融合成氦的核融合反應。
factTeen.en: The most abundant and lightest element in the universe; the Sun gets its energy by fusing hydrogen into helium. Hydrogen gas is lighter than air and can serve as an energy source for fuel cells.

useTeen.zh: 氫氣比空氣輕,可以當燃料電池的能量來源。

factHigh.zh: 原子序 1,宇宙中含量最多的元素;恆星(如太陽)內部的核融合把氫轉變成氦並釋放能量。
factHigh.en: Atomic number 1 and the most abundant element in the universe; fusion inside stars such as the Sun turns hydrogen into helium and releases energy. It is a fuel for fuel cells and a feedstock for ammonia synthesis and oil refining.

useHigh.zh: 燃料電池的燃料;工業上用於合成氨與石油精煉。

fact.zh: 吸了氦氣聲音會變成唐老鴨!它比空氣輕,也不會燒起來。
fact.en: Breathe it in and your voice sounds like a duck! Lighter than air and never burns.

use.zh: 用來灌氣球、冷卻醫院的核磁共振儀。

factTeen.zh: 氦氣比空氣輕,也不會燃燒;吸入後聲音會變尖。
factTeen.en: Helium is lighter than air and does not burn; breathing it makes your voice sound high. It fills balloons and cools hospital MRI machines.

useTeen.zh: 用來灌氣球,並冷卻醫院的核磁共振儀。

factHigh.zh: 沸點最低的元素(約 4.2 K),最外層為填滿的 1s²,化學性質極不活潑。
factHigh.en: The element with the lowest boiling point (about 4.2 K), with a filled 1s² shell and extremely inert chemistry. Liquid helium cools the superconducting magnets of MRI machines, and helium fills balloons and airships.

useHigh.zh: 液態氦用於超導磁鐵(如核磁共振儀)的冷卻,也用作氣球與飛船的填充氣體。

fact.zh: 最輕的金屬,輕到可以浮在水上。
fact.en: The lightest metal. It powers phone and electric car batteries.

use.zh: 手機和電動車的電池都靠它。

factTeen.zh: 最輕的金屬,密度比水小,會浮在水面上。
factTeen.en: The lightest metal, less dense than water, so it floats. It is a key material in the lithium batteries of phones and electric cars.

useTeen.zh: 手機與電動車的鋰電池材料。

factHigh.zh: 密度最小的金屬(約 0.53 g/cm³),屬於鹼金屬,價電子組態為 2s¹。
factHigh.en: The least dense metal (about 0.53 g/cm³), an alkali metal with the valence configuration 2s¹. It is a key material in lithium-ion batteries.

useHigh.zh: 鋰離子電池的關鍵材料。

fact.zh: 鉛筆芯和鑽石都是碳,排列方式不同就差好多!
fact.en: Pencil lead and diamond are both carbon, just arranged differently. Carbon is the backbone of life.

use.zh: 所有生物都含有碳,碳是生命的骨架。

factTeen.zh: 鉛筆芯的石墨和鑽石都是碳,因為原子排列方式不同,性質差很多。
factTeen.en: Pencil graphite and diamond are both carbon; the atoms are arranged differently, so their properties differ greatly. All living things contain carbon, the backbone of organic compounds.

useTeen.zh: 所有生物體都含有碳,它是有機化合物的骨架。

factHigh.zh: 同素異形體包括鑽石、石墨、富勒烯與石墨烯;碳能形成穩定的長鏈與環,是有機化學的基礎。
factHigh.en: Its allotropes include diamond, graphite, fullerenes and graphene; carbon forms stable chains and rings, the basis of organic chemistry. It is the backbone of biomolecules and the main element of fossil fuels.

useHigh.zh: 生物分子與有機化合物的骨架,化石燃料的主要成分。

fact.zh: 空氣有 78% 是氮氣。
fact.en: 78% of air is nitrogen. Plants need it to grow, so fertilizer contains it.

use.zh: 植物需要氮才能長得綠油油,肥料裡就有它。

factTeen.zh: 氮氣約占空氣體積的 78%。
factTeen.en: Nitrogen gas makes up about 78% of air by volume. Plants need nitrogen to grow, which is why fertilizers contain it.

useTeen.zh: 植物需要氮來生長,肥料裡含有氮。

factHigh.zh: 氮氣(N₂)約占空氣體積的 78%,N≡N 叄鍵很強,所以化學性質不活潑。
factHigh.en: Nitrogen gas (N₂) makes up about 78% of air by volume; the N≡N triple bond is very strong, so it is unreactive. Nitrogen is part of amino acids and DNA, and the Haber process turns it into ammonia for fertilizer.

useHigh.zh: 胺基酸與 DNA 的組成元素;哈伯法合成氨是肥料的來源。

fact.zh: 我們呼吸靠它!空氣約有 21% 是氧氣。
fact.en: We breathe it! Fire needs oxygen too, so covering a candle puts it out.

use.zh: 火要燃燒也需要氧氣,所以蓋住蠟燭火就熄了。

factTeen.zh: 氧氣約占空氣體積的 21%,是我們呼吸所需要的氣體。
factTeen.en: Oxygen makes up about 21% of air by volume and is the gas we need to breathe. Burning also needs oxygen, which is why covering a candle puts the flame out.

useTeen.zh: 燃燒需要氧氣,所以蓋住蠟燭,火就會熄滅。

factHigh.zh: 地殼中含量最多的元素;O₂ 約占空氣體積的 21%,是有氧呼吸與燃燒的氧化劑。
factHigh.en: The most abundant element in Earth's crust; O₂ is about 21% of air by volume and the oxidant in aerobic respiration and combustion. It is also used in steelmaking and medical oxygen supply.

useHigh.zh: 燃燒與呼吸作用的氧化劑,也用於煉鋼與醫療供氧。

fact.zh: 牙膏裡的氟可以讓牙齒更堅固,防蛀牙。
fact.en: Fluoride in toothpaste makes teeth stronger. It is the most reactive nonmetal.

use.zh: 它是最活潑的非金屬元素。

factTeen.zh: 牙膏裡的氟化物能強化牙齒,幫助預防蛀牙。
factTeen.en: The fluoride in toothpaste strengthens teeth and helps prevent cavities. Fluorine is the most reactive nonmetal.

useTeen.zh: 氟是最活潑的非金屬元素。

factHigh.zh: 電負度最大(約 4.0)的元素,F₂ 是最強的氧化劑之一。
factHigh.en: The most electronegative element (about 4.0); F₂ is one of the strongest oxidizing agents. Fluorides are used in toothpaste, refrigerants and Teflon (PTFE).

useHigh.zh: 氟化物用於牙膏、冷媒與鐵氟龍(PTFE)。

fact.zh: 霓虹燈的紅橙色光就是氖氣發出來的。
fact.en: The red-orange glow of neon signs! It almost never makes compounds.

use.zh: 氖幾乎不跟別的元素交朋友。

factTeen.zh: 氖氣通電時會發出紅橙色的光,霓虹燈招牌就是利用這一點。
factTeen.en: Neon glows red-orange when an electric current passes through it, which is how neon signs work. Neon is very stable and hardly reacts with other elements.

useTeen.zh: 氖的化學性質非常穩定,幾乎不和其他元素反應。

factHigh.zh: 稀有氣體,放電時發出紅橙色光;最外層為填滿的 2s²2p⁶。
factHigh.en: A noble gas that glows red-orange in a discharge, with the filled outer shell 2s²2p⁶. It is used in neon signs and helium-neon lasers.

useHigh.zh: 霓虹燈與氦氖雷射。

fact.zh: 食鹽的一半是鈉。純鈉丟進水裡會劇烈冒泡!
fact.en: Half of table salt. Pure sodium fizzes wildly in water!

use.zh: 鈉是很軟的銀色金屬,可以用刀切開。

factTeen.zh: 食鹽(氯化鈉)裡有鈉。純的鈉很活潑,放進水中會劇烈反應。
factTeen.en: Table salt (sodium chloride) contains sodium. Pure sodium is very reactive and reacts violently with water. It is a soft silvery metal that can be cut with a knife.

useTeen.zh: 鈉是柔軟的銀白色金屬,可以用刀切開。

factHigh.zh: 鹼金屬,價電子組態 3s¹,極易失去電子;與水劇烈反應生成 NaOH 與 H₂。
factHigh.en: An alkali metal with the valence configuration 3s¹ that loses its electron very readily; it reacts violently with water to give NaOH and H₂. It is used in sodium vapor lamps and the chemical industry, and Na⁺ ions help keep body fluids in balance.

useHigh.zh: 鈉蒸氣燈與化學工業;鈉離子是體內維持體液平衡的重要離子。

fact.zh: 煙火和閃光燈裡的白亮光來自鎂燃燒。
fact.en: Burning magnesium makes brilliant white light. Chlorophyll has a magnesium atom at its center.

use.zh: 葉綠素的中心就是鎂原子。

factTeen.zh: 鎂燃燒時發出耀眼的白光,所以煙火與閃光燈用它。
factTeen.en: Magnesium burns with a dazzling white light, which is why fireworks and flash lamps use it. A magnesium atom sits at the center of chlorophyll.

useTeen.zh: 葉綠素的中心就是一個鎂原子。

factHigh.zh: 鹼土金屬,燃燒時發出耀眼的白光(2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO)。
factHigh.en: An alkaline earth metal that burns with a dazzling white light (2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO). It sits at the center of chlorophyll, and light magnesium alloys are used in laptop cases and car parts.

useHigh.zh: 葉綠素的中心原子;輕質的鎂合金用於筆電外殼與汽車零件。

fact.zh: 鋁罐、鋁箔紙都是它,又輕又不容易生鏽。
fact.en: Cans and foil are aluminium: light and rust-resistant. The most common metal in Earth's crust.

use.zh: 地殼中最多的金屬元素。

factTeen.zh: 鋁罐和鋁箔都是鋁做的,它又輕又不容易生鏽。
factTeen.en: Aluminum cans and foil are made of aluminum, which is light and does not rust easily. It is the most abundant metal in Earth's crust.

useTeen.zh: 鋁是地殼中含量最多的金屬元素。

factHigh.zh: 表面會形成緻密的氧化鋁薄膜,保護內部不再氧化;是地殼中含量最多的金屬元素。
factHigh.en: A dense aluminum oxide film forms on its surface and protects the metal beneath; it is the most abundant metal in Earth's crust. It is used for packaging, building and aerospace structures, and can be recycled.

useHigh.zh: 包裝、建材與航太結構材料,可回收再利用。

fact.zh: 沙子和玻璃的主角,電腦晶片也是矽做的!
fact.en: Sand, glass and computer chips are made from silicon.

use.zh: 台灣的半導體產業就靠它。

factTeen.zh: 沙子與玻璃的主要成分是矽的化合物,電腦晶片也用矽製成。
factTeen.en: Sand and glass are mainly compounds of silicon, and computer chips are made of silicon too. Taiwan's semiconductor industry relies heavily on silicon.

useTeen.zh: 台灣的半導體產業大量使用矽。

factHigh.zh: 類金屬,是半導體;SiO₂ 是沙子與玻璃的主要成分,矽是地殼中含量第二多的元素。
factHigh.en: A metalloid and semiconductor; SiO₂ is the main component of sand and glass, and silicon is the second most abundant element in Earth's crust. It is the substrate material of integrated circuits and solar cells.

useHigh.zh: 積體電路與太陽能電池的基板材料。

fact.zh: 火柴頭裡有磷,摩擦就會點燃。
fact.en: Match heads contain phosphorus. Bones, teeth and DNA need it too.

use.zh: 骨頭和牙齒需要磷,DNA 也含有磷。

factTeen.zh: 火柴盒側面的塗層含有紅磷,摩擦時能引燃火柴頭。
factTeen.en: The strip on the side of a matchbox contains red phosphorus, which ignites the match head when struck. Bones, teeth and DNA all contain phosphorus.

useTeen.zh: 骨頭、牙齒與 DNA 都含有磷。

factHigh.zh: 白磷會自燃,紅磷較穩定;磷是 DNA、RNA 與 ATP 的組成元素。
factHigh.en: White phosphorus ignites spontaneously while red phosphorus is more stable; phosphorus is part of DNA, RNA and ATP. It is used for phosphate fertilizers, matches and phosphoric acid.

useHigh.zh: 肥料(磷肥)、火柴與磷酸的原料。

fact.zh: 溫泉的特殊味道和火山口黃色結晶都是硫。
fact.en: Hot-spring smell and yellow volcano crystals are sulfur.

use.zh: 硫黃曾被用來做火藥和橡膠硬化。

factTeen.zh: 溫泉的特殊氣味與火山口的黃色結晶都和硫有關。
factTeen.en: The smell of hot springs and the yellow crystals around volcanic vents come from sulfur. Sulfur was used to make gunpowder and to harden rubber.

useTeen.zh: 硫黃曾用來製作火藥和硬化橡膠。

factHigh.zh: 黃色固體,常見分子為 S₈ 皇冠環;燃燒生成 SO₂。
factHigh.en: A yellow solid whose usual molecule is the S₈ crown ring; it burns to give SO₂. It is used for sulfuric acid, rubber vulcanization and gunpowder.

useHigh.zh: 製造硫酸、橡膠硫化與火藥。

fact.zh: 游泳池消毒用的氯,和鈉結合就變成食鹽。
fact.en: Pools are disinfected with chlorine; with sodium it makes salt. Chlorine gas itself is toxic.

use.zh: 單獨的氯氣是有毒的黃綠色氣體。

factTeen.zh: 游泳池用氯來消毒,氯和鈉結合成食鹽。
factTeen.en: Swimming pools are disinfected with chlorine, and chlorine combined with sodium makes table salt. Chlorine gas on its own is a poisonous yellow-green gas.

useTeen.zh: 單質氯氣是有毒的黃綠色氣體。

factHigh.zh: 鹵素,Cl₂ 為黃綠色有毒氣體,氧化力強;Cl⁻ 是食鹽與胃酸的成分。
factHigh.en: A halogen; Cl₂ is a poisonous yellow-green gas with strong oxidizing power, and Cl⁻ is part of table salt and stomach acid. It is used to disinfect water and to make PVC and bleach.

useHigh.zh: 飲水與泳池消毒、製造 PVC 與漂白劑。

fact.zh: 燈泡裡充的氣體,保護燈絲不被燒壞。
fact.en: Filled in light bulbs to protect the filament. The third most common gas in air.

use.zh: 空氣裡排第三多的氣體。

factTeen.zh: 燈泡裡充入氬氣,可以保護燈絲不被燒壞。
factTeen.en: Light bulbs are filled with argon to protect the filament from burning out. Argon is the third most abundant gas in air.

useTeen.zh: 氬是空氣中含量第三多的氣體。

factHigh.zh: 稀有氣體,約占空氣體積的 0.93%,化學性質極不活潑。
factHigh.en: A noble gas making up about 0.93% of air by volume, chemically extremely inert. It is used as a shielding gas for welding and in light bulbs.

useHigh.zh: 焊接與燈泡的保護氣體。

fact.zh: 香蕉含有很多鉀,對肌肉和心臟很重要。
fact.en: Bananas are rich in potassium, which muscles and hearts need.

use.zh: 鉀比鈉更活潑,碰水會燒起紫色火焰。

factTeen.zh: 香蕉含有很多鉀,鉀對肌肉與心臟的運作很重要。
factTeen.en: Bananas contain a lot of potassium, which is important for muscles and the heart. Potassium is more reactive than sodium and burns with a lilac flame in water.

useTeen.zh: 鉀比鈉更活潑,遇水會產生淡紫色的火焰。

factHigh.zh: 鹼金屬,價電子組態 4s¹;與水劇烈反應並使火焰呈淡紫色。K⁺ 是維持細胞膜電位的重要離子。
factHigh.en: An alkali metal with the valence configuration 4s¹ that reacts violently with water with a lilac flame; K⁺ is an important ion for the membrane potential of cells. It is used in potash fertilizer and is an electrolyte needed by nerves and muscles.

useHigh.zh: 鉀肥,以及神經與肌肉運作所需的電解質。

fact.zh: 骨頭、牙齒、貝殼和蛋殼都含有鈣,多喝牛奶補充鈣!
fact.en: Bones, teeth, shells and eggshells contain calcium. Drink milk!

use.zh: 石灰岩和粉筆也是鈣的化合物。

factTeen.zh: 骨頭、牙齒、貝殼與蛋殼都含有鈣。
factTeen.en: Bones, teeth, seashells and eggshells all contain calcium. Limestone and chalk are calcium compounds.

useTeen.zh: 石灰岩與粉筆是鈣的化合物。

factHigh.zh: 鹼土金屬;Ca²⁺ 是骨骼與牙齒(羥基磷灰石)的主要成分,也參與肌肉收縮與血液凝固。
factHigh.en: An alkaline earth metal; Ca²⁺ is the main component of bones and teeth (hydroxyapatite) and also takes part in muscle contraction and blood clotting. Cement, lime and calcium supplements are made from CaCO₃.

useHigh.zh: 水泥、石灰與補鈣劑的原料(來自 CaCO₃)。

fact.zh: 又輕又強壯,眼鏡框和人工關節常用鈦。
fact.en: Strong and light: used in glasses frames and artificial joints.

factTeen.zh: 鈦又輕又堅固,常用於眼鏡框與人工關節。
factTeen.en: Titanium is light and strong, and is often used for eyeglass frames and artificial joints.

factHigh.zh: 強度高、密度小,表面的氧化膜使它耐腐蝕,與人體組織相容性佳。
factHigh.en: High strength and low density; its oxide film resists corrosion and it is well tolerated by body tissue.

fact.zh: 讓水龍頭亮晶晶的電鍍就是鉻,不鏽鋼也含鉻。
fact.en: Chrome plating makes faucets shine, and stainless steel contains chromium.

factTeen.zh: 水龍頭的鍍層是鉻,不鏽鋼也含有鉻。
factTeen.en: The shiny plating on faucets is chromium, and stainless steel contains chromium too.

factHigh.zh: 銀亮的硬金屬,表面的氧化鉻膜使它耐腐蝕;不鏽鋼含鉻 10.5% 以上。
factHigh.en: A bright, hard metal whose chromium oxide film resists corrosion; stainless steel contains more than 10.5% chromium.

fact.zh: 地球核心主要是鐵,血液裡的血紅素也含鐵。
fact.en: Earth's core is mostly iron, and so is the heart of your blood's hemoglobin. Iron rusts in damp air.

use.zh: 鐵碰到水和空氣會生鏽。

factTeen.zh: 地球的核心主要是鐵,血液中的血紅素也含有鐵。
factTeen.en: Earth's core is mostly iron, and the hemoglobin in blood contains iron too. Iron rusts when it meets water and air.

useTeen.zh: 鐵遇到水和空氣會生鏽。

factHigh.zh: 地球內核與外核的主要成分;血紅素中的 Fe²⁺ 可以和氧結合。
factHigh.en: The main component of Earth's inner and outer core; the Fe²⁺ in hemoglobin binds oxygen. It is the main component of steel, and in damp air it oxidizes to rust (Fe₂O₃·nH₂O).

useHigh.zh: 鋼鐵的主要成分;鐵在潮濕空氣中氧化生成鐵鏽(Fe₂O₃·nH₂O)。

fact.zh: 硬幣和不鏽鋼裡常見的銀白色金屬。
fact.en: A silvery metal in coins and stainless steel.

factTeen.zh: 硬幣與不鏽鋼裡常見的銀白色金屬。
factTeen.en: A silvery-white metal common in coins and stainless steel.

factHigh.zh: 銀白色的鐵磁性金屬,耐腐蝕;常用於合金、電鍍與充電電池。
factHigh.en: A silvery-white ferromagnetic metal that resists corrosion; often used in alloys, electroplating and rechargeable batteries.

fact.zh: 紅色的金屬,導電很好,電線都用銅。
fact.en: A red metal that conducts electricity well, so wires use copper.

use.zh: 銅製的硬幣表面久了會變綠色(銅綠)。

factTeen.zh: 銅是紅色的金屬,導電性很好,電線大多用銅製成。
factTeen.en: Copper is a red metal and a very good conductor, so most electric wires are made of copper. Copper objects slowly turn green on the surface (verdigris).

useTeen.zh: 銅製品表面久了會產生綠色的銅綠。

factHigh.zh: 電導率僅次於銀的金屬,電線的主要材料;表面久了形成綠色的鹼式碳酸銅(銅綠)。
factHigh.en: A metal whose electrical conductivity is second only to silver, the main material of electric wires; its surface slowly forms green basic copper carbonate (verdigris). It is used in wires, pipes and alloys such as brass and bronze.

useHigh.zh: 電線、水管與合金(黃銅、青銅)。

fact.zh: 鍍在鐵上防止生鏽(鍍鋅),也是乾電池的材料。
fact.en: Coats iron against rust (galvanizing) and is used in batteries.

factTeen.zh: 鐵表面鍍鋅可以防止生鏽,鋅也是乾電池的材料。
factTeen.en: Coating iron with zinc (galvanizing) prevents rust, and zinc is also a material of dry cells.

factHigh.zh: 活性比鐵大,鍍在鋼鐵表面可作為犧牲陽極;是乾電池的負極材料。
factHigh.en: More reactive than iron, so a zinc coating on steel acts as a sacrificial anode; it is the negative electrode material of dry cells.

fact.zh: 常溫下是紅棕色液體的非金屬,味道很刺鼻。
fact.en: One of only two elements that are liquid at room temperature (with mercury).

factTeen.zh: 溴是常溫下呈紅棕色液體的非金屬,氣味刺鼻。
factTeen.en: Bromine is a nonmetal that is a red-brown liquid at room temperature, with a sharp smell.

factHigh.zh: 鹵素,常溫為紅棕色液體(Br₂),易揮發且有毒。
factHigh.en: A halogen that is a red-brown liquid (Br₂) at room temperature; volatile and toxic.

fact.zh: 有些閃光燈和雷射使用氪氣。
fact.en: Used in some flash lamps and lasers.

factTeen.zh: 有些閃光燈與雷射使用氪氣。
factTeen.en: Some flash lamps and lasers use krypton gas.

factHigh.zh: 稀有氣體,放電時發出白光;化學性質極不活潑。
factHigh.en: A noble gas that glows white in a discharge; chemically extremely inert.

fact.zh: 導電導熱最好的金屬,也拿來做飾品與餐具。
fact.en: The best conductor of heat and electricity; used for jewelry and cutlery.

factTeen.zh: 銀是導電、導熱最好的金屬,也用來做飾品和餐具。
factTeen.en: Silver conducts electricity and heat better than any other metal, and is also used for jewelry and tableware.

factHigh.zh: 所有金屬中電導率與熱導率最高;與含硫物質反應生成黑色的硫化銀。
factHigh.en: It has the highest electrical and thermal conductivity of all metals; it reacts with sulfur compounds to form black silver sulfide.

fact.zh: 罐頭的「馬口鐵」就是鐵皮鍍上一層錫。
fact.en: Tin cans are iron coated with a thin layer of tin.

factTeen.zh: 罐頭的「馬口鐵」是在鐵皮上鍍一層錫。
factTeen.en: The "tinplate" of food cans is sheet iron coated with a layer of tin.

factHigh.zh: 熔點低(約 232 °C)的軟金屬;鍍在鋼鐵表面可防鏽(馬口鐵)。
factHigh.en: A soft metal with a low melting point (about 232 °C); a tin coating protects steel from rusting (tinplate).

fact.zh: 碘酒用來消毒傷口,海帶富含碘。
fact.en: Iodine disinfects cuts, and seaweed is rich in it.

factTeen.zh: 碘酒用來消毒傷口,海帶含有很多碘。
factTeen.en: Tincture of iodine is used to disinfect wounds, and kelp is rich in iodine.

factHigh.zh: 鹵素,紫黑色固體,容易昇華;人體需要碘來合成甲狀腺素。
factHigh.en: A halogen, a violet-black solid that sublimes readily; the body needs iodine to make thyroid hormone.

fact.zh: 汽車的亮白色氙氣大燈。
fact.en: Makes the bright white light of xenon car headlights.

factTeen.zh: 汽車的亮白色氙氣大燈使用氙。
factTeen.en: The bright white xenon headlamps of cars use xenon.

factHigh.zh: 稀有氣體,放電時發出明亮的藍白光;是最容易形成化合物的稀有氣體之一。
factHigh.en: A noble gas that glows bright blue-white in a discharge; one of the noble gases that most readily forms compounds.

fact.zh: 熔點最高的金屬,老式燈泡的燈絲就是鎢。
fact.en: The highest melting point of any metal: old light-bulb filaments.

factTeen.zh: 鎢是熔點最高的金屬,老式燈泡的燈絲就是鎢。
factTeen.en: Tungsten has the highest melting point of any metal, and the filament of old-style light bulbs is tungsten.

factHigh.zh: 熔點最高的金屬(約 3422 °C),因此用於白熾燈絲與高溫合金。
factHigh.en: The metal with the highest melting point (about 3422 °C), so it is used for incandescent filaments and high-temperature alloys.

fact.zh: 珍貴又不易變質的白金,常用在首飾與催化器。
fact.en: Precious and non-reactive; used in jewelry and catalytic converters.

factTeen.zh: 鉑(白金)珍貴又不容易變質,常用在首飾與汽車的觸媒轉化器。
factTeen.en: Platinum is precious and does not tarnish, and is used in jewelry and in the catalytic converters of cars.

factHigh.zh: 化學穩定性很高的貴金屬,也是優良的催化劑(如汽車觸媒轉化器)。
factHigh.en: A noble metal of very high chemical stability and an excellent catalyst (as in car catalytic converters).

fact.zh: 黃澄澄的黃金,幾乎不會生鏽,幾千年前的金飾依然閃亮。
fact.en: Shiny gold hardly ever tarnishes, so ancient gold still gleams.

factTeen.zh: 金幾乎不會生鏽,幾千年前的金飾到現在依然閃亮。
factTeen.en: Gold hardly ever rusts, so gold jewelry made thousands of years ago still shines.

factHigh.zh: 化學性質極穩定、延展性極佳的金屬;只溶於王水等少數溶液。
factHigh.en: A chemically very stable and highly ductile metal that dissolves only in a few solutions such as aqua regia.

fact.zh: 唯一常溫下是液體的金屬,但有毒,舊式溫度計裡有它。
fact.en: The only metal that is liquid at room temperature, but toxic.

factTeen.zh: 汞是唯一在常溫下呈液態的金屬,但有毒,舊式溫度計裡有它。
factTeen.en: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature, but it is toxic; old thermometers contained it.

factHigh.zh: 常溫下唯一呈液態的金屬,蒸氣有毒;已逐漸被其他材料取代。
factHigh.en: The only metal that is liquid at room temperature; its vapor is toxic, and it is being replaced by other materials.

fact.zh: 又重又軟的金屬,但對身體有害,現在很少用了。
fact.en: Heavy and soft but harmful to health, so it is rarely used now.

factTeen.zh: 鉛又重又軟,但對身體有害,現在已經很少使用。
factTeen.en: Lead is heavy and soft, but it is harmful to the body, so it is rarely used now.

factHigh.zh: 密度大、質地軟的重金屬,有毒;曾用於汽油添加劑與水管,現已大幅限制。
factHigh.en: A dense, soft and toxic heavy metal; once used in gasoline additives and water pipes, but now heavily restricted.

fact.zh: 核能發電的燃料。
fact.en: Fuel for nuclear power plants.

factTeen.zh: 鈾是核能發電的燃料。
factTeen.en: Uranium is the fuel of nuclear power plants.

factHigh.zh: 具放射性的重元素,鈾-235 可發生核分裂,是核能發電的燃料。
factHigh.en: A radioactive heavy element; uranium-235 can undergo fission and is the fuel of nuclear power.
